name: Netherlands
description:
A progressive and efficient nation known for its bicycles, windmills, and tulips. The Netherlands offers excellent work-life balance, outstanding infrastructure, and a welcoming expat community in Amsterdam.

## Key Highlights
- Excellent work-life balance and quality of life
- World-class infrastructure and public services
- Welcoming expat community with English-friendly culture
longdescription: The Netherlands is a Western European nation known for efficiency, progressive values, and exceptional quality of life. Amsterdam, the capital, is a vibrant and international city with world-class museums, canals, cycling infrastructure, and a thriving cultural scene. The country is famously flat, crisscrossed by bicycle paths and canals, making cycling the primary transportation. Dutch people generally speak excellent English, making it accessible for foreign residents. The economy is highly developed and diverse, with strong sectors in finance, agriculture, manufacturing, and technology. The Netherlands ranks among the world's most innovative economies. Healthcare is excellent and well-organized. The education system is highly regarded. The cost of living is moderate to high, particularly in Amsterdam and other major cities. Work-life balance is exceptional by international standards, with strong labor protections and emphasis on personal time. The Dutch are known for directness and egalitarian values. Public services and infrastructure are world-class. The country offers numerous visa options for skilled workers, entrepreneurs, and investors. The flat landscape and excellent cycling infrastructure promote outdoor recreation and a healthy lifestyle. Challenges include high housing costs in major cities and competition for accommodation. The Netherlands combines progressive values, efficiency, English-friendly environment, exceptional infrastructure, work-life balance, and cultural openness, making it highly attractive to international professionals and families.

visas.name: For highly skilled (Netherlands)
visas.description: For highly skilled workers from outside the EU/EEA who have a job offer from a recognized Dutch sponsor.

visas.name: For innovative entrepreneurs (Netherlands)
visas.description: For innovative entrepreneurs who want to launch their startup in the Netherlands.

visas.name: The Dutch family (Netherlands)
visas.description: The Dutch family reunification permit allows non-EU family members of legal Dutch residents to join them in the Netherlands. The sponsor must meet minimum income requirements and provide adequate accommodation.

visas.name: The Dutch student (Netherlands)
visas.description: The Dutch student residence permit (MVV + IND permit) allows non-EU/EEA nationals enrolled at a Dutch higher education institution to live and study in the Netherlands for the duration of their programme.

visas.name: The Dutch self-employed (Netherlands)
visas.description: The Dutch self-employed residence permit (equivalent to a digital nomad visa) allows non-EU freelancers and remote entrepreneurs to live and work in the Netherlands, assessed via a points-based system covering experience, business plan, and Dutch economic contribution.
benefits: Live and work as a freelancer in the Netherlands

visas.name: The Dutch Orientation (Netherlands)
visas.description: The Dutch Orientation Year (Zoekjaar) permit allows recent non-EU graduates from recognised universities to stay in the Netherlands for one year to find work or start a business.
benefits: Job search in the Netherlands after graduation
Right to work during permit period

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Children of Dutch citizen parent(s) acquire Dutch citizenship automatically at birth.

Naturalization.desc:
**Requirements:** 5 years legal residence (EU/EEA: 2 years), Dutch language (A2 level), integration, renunciation of other citizenship (dual citizenship limited).

**Processing:** Through IND, 3-6 months.

Spouse and Family.desc: Married couples where one is Dutch may have accelerated naturalization after 2 years marriage.

Limited Dual Citizenship.desc: Generally not permitted, but Dutch-born children of naturalized parents may retain dual citizenship until age 22 to choose.

tax_advice:
- Netherlands has progressive income tax (19.55% to 49.5%)
- Corporate tax rate is 23% (19% for profits up to €200k for small entities)
- VAT at 21% (reduced rates of 9%, 6%, and 0%)
- Non-residents taxed on Dutch-source income and worldwide Dutch-originating income
- Ruling system (APA/RULING) allows advance tax agreements
- Capital gains from regular investments may be exempt
- Substance requirements critical for tax residency determination
- Employer and employee social contributions required
local_tips:
- Dutch very widely spoken; English nearly universal but Dutch appreciated
- Bureaucracy efficient; register with gemeente (municipality) immediately
- Cycling culture dominant; invest in good bike and follow traffic laws
- Cost of living high but reasonable for quality of life; budget €1,500-2,000/month
- Rental market competitive; start searching early through established sites
- Healthcare: Mandatory insurance; deductible system common
- Weather cool and grey; embrace cycling and indoor culture
